_comment: Probes for the five practice-layer skills, in the shape probes.example.json documents.
THE NON-TRIGGERING PROBES ARE THE HARD HALF, AND THESE FIVE SKILLS ARE EACH OTHER'S NEAREST
NEIGHBOURS. That is not an accident of naming -- they were carved out of one set of documents,
so they share a vocabulary almost word for word. verification-before-claiming and
git-comparison-choice both answer 'is this actually true'. reversibility-before-destructive and
handoff-discipline both answer 'before you do the thing you cannot take back'. Every negative
below is aimed at one of the other three, and _neighbours names which. A negative aimed at the
weather would measure a confusion nobody was going to make and report an accuracy none of these
has earned.
One easy negative is kept per skill as a floor, and it is labelled as such rather than left to
look like a real defence. Four and four is the convention, not a rule the script enforces.
Phrasing is varied deliberately: four rewordings of one sentence measure one thing four times.
TWO DEVIATIONS BELONG TO agent-orchestration, AND BOTH ARE DELIBERATE. It keeps NO floor
negative: it is the only skill here with four nearest neighbours rather than three -- the other
four all concern reviewing, comparing, destroying or writing up work an agent produced -- so the
slot the other sets spend on a definition request is spent on the fourth neighbour instead. The
floor is already established four times over above it, and a fifth definition request would
measure a confusion nobody was going to make.
AND THE OTHER FOUR SETS DO NOT YET CARRY A NEGATIVE AIMED AT agent-orchestration, which is a
known gap rather than a judgement that none is needed. It arrived as the fifth skill and became
a neighbour to all four in the same move; the nearest collision is with
verification-before-claiming, since both concern reviewing output. Recorded here rather than
closed quietly, because a defence measured in one direction only reports an accuracy the pair
has not earned.
'exempt' is empty and should stay that way here. It is the one place a coverage gate can be
silenced, so an entry without a stated reason is a silencer rather than a decision -- the
loader rejects one.

triggering: You said the fix works. How would I know that from the outside?
This suite is green. Should I believe it, or is it green for the wrong reason?
Before you write the function, tell me what would prove it is right.
That scan reported no findings in about a second. Is that a pass?
non_triggering: Two diffs of this branch disagree about how many files it touched. Which one is right?
I am about to drop the staging tables. Walk me through making that recoverable first.
I am nearly out of room in this window -- write up where we got to.
Rename this variable so it matches the one in the caller.
_neighbours: 1 -> git-comparison-choice: same subject (is this claim true) but the instrument is a diff, and the answer is a choice between comparisons rather than a choice of reviewer.
2 -> reversibility-before-destructive: 'prove it first' is the shared phrase; here it is proving a SET before a delete, not proving a claim before an assertion.
3 -> handoff-discipline: a handoff status section is full of verified-versus-not language, which is the likeliest collision of all four.
4 -> ordinary editing work, kept as one easy negative to floor the set.

triggering: Write me a script that clears out the orphaned rows. I want to be able to undo it.
The backup finished and exited zero. Is that enough before I overwrite the store?
How do I stage this bulk update so a partial failure is survivable?
I need to delete about half of these files. What has to happen before I do?
non_triggering: Is this branch's work already in the base branch, or am I about to lose it?
Design the check that proves the migration produced the numbers it claims.
Stop here and write this up cleanly so a new session can carry on tomorrow.
Explain what a write-ahead log is.
_neighbours: 1 -> git-comparison-choice: a keep-or-delete decision, which is a delete decision, but the hard part is which comparison answers it -- not the rollback.
2 -> verification-before-claiming: 'design the check' is the shared trigger; the subject is a claim about numbers, not an irreversible step.
3 -> handoff-discipline: both fire at the end of a piece of work and both say 'before you do the thing you cannot take back'. The tell is that nothing is being destroyed.
4 -> a definition request, kept as the floor negative.

triggering: Wrap this session up for a fresh one -- I will pick it up in a new window.
Can you write down where we are so somebody else can take it from here?
I am running low on context. Do we compact or hand off?
Note down what we decided and what is still open, then stop.
non_triggering: Give me a one-line progress update -- are you halfway through the refactor?
The changes were merged. Confirm they are actually on the base branch.
Before you clear the export directory, prove which files are safe to remove.
Summarise this design document for the team.
_neighbours: 1 -> nothing in this set, and that is the point: a mid-task progress report is what this skill is most often mistaken FOR, and it must decline rather than write a document about an inconsistent state.
2 -> git-comparison-choice: 'confirm it landed' is a status claim, which is exactly the sentence a handoff would carry -- but the question asked is which comparison settles it.
3 -> reversibility-before-destructive: 'prove it before you do it' phrased identically, aimed at a delete.
4 -> a generic summarisation request, which any writing skill over-claims. The floor negative.

triggering: Is it safe to delete this branch, or is some of it still only here?
The push said everything was up to date but the file is not on the remote. What happened?
Compared one way this branch adds twelve files, compared the other way three. Explain.
It was squash-merged. Why does the merged-ness check still say no?
non_triggering: Rank the ways of reviewing this output from most to least independent.
The branch is dead. Delete it and the worktree, but make that reversible.
Record the branch and commit we are on so the next session lands in the right tree.
What does a fast-forward merge mean?
_neighbours: 1 -> verification-before-claiming: the independence ladder is its content, and both skills are about whether an answer can be trusted. Nothing here is a comparison.
2 -> reversibility-before-destructive: the delete decision is already made, so what is wanted is the recovery window rather than the evidence.
3 -> handoff-discipline: branch and commit are shared vocabulary, and the resume block is where they appear -- but this is a request to write a handoff field, not to compare anything.
4 -> a definition request about git itself, kept as the floor negative.

triggering: I want one agent to draft this and a second to check it. What should the checker not be allowed to see?
My review panel passes everything. Three judges, all agreeing, and the scores only ever go up.
Two subagents both edited the registry and half of the first one's work is gone. How should I have split this?
Set up the fan-out for this audit — who plans, who fetches, who scores, and where does the run stop?
non_triggering: The auditor scored this a five. How would I know from the outside that the score is right?
Two agents worked this branch and the two diffs disagree about what it adds. Which comparison settles it?
Before the cleanup agent runs over the export directory, make that recoverable.
Three parallel sessions have been on this all week. Write up where each one got to so tomorrow's window can carry on.
_neighbours: 1 -> verification-before-claiming: THE NEAREST NEIGHBOUR, and the whole vocabulary is shared -- auditor, score, from the outside. The boundary is that this probe asks whether ONE claim is true, which is answered by choosing a check whose mistakes are independent of the claim; this skill would answer a different question, namely how to arrange the roles so that a score is worth reading at all. Structuring roles versus adjudicating a claim.

2 -> git-comparison-choice: 'two agents' is this skill's own subject matter and is a decoy here. Nothing is being decomposed and no role is being assigned; the question is which of two comparisons answers what the branch adds, and it would have the same answer with one author.

3 -> reversibility-before-destructive: an agent is doing the work, which is the shared surface, but the ask is the recovery window for a step that cannot be taken back. No split, no panel, no write-scope table -- and the answer is the same whether a person or an agent runs it.

4 -> handoff-discipline: 'three parallel sessions' is the closest this set comes to a trap, because parallel work is exactly what this skill plans. The tell is the deliverable: a document for a later reader, not a decomposition for a dispatcher. The work has already happened, so there is nothing left to assign.
